body: Hexagon US Federal, Inc. (HexFed) leased two bays in a building on Dunlop Boulevard in Huntsville from a related company, Intergraph Unimproved Properties, LLC, in 2015. A 2016 amended lease put both bays on a five-year term but stated the maximum rent for one bay only for 12 months. CBS Holdings, LLC bought the building in November 2016 and became the landlord. In July 2019 CBS Holdings first asserted that the bay's term had been 12 months; HexFed disputed that and stayed at the lease rate. In December 2020 HexFed sent notice renewing the lease, and CBS Holdings rejected it, citing among other reasons that the notice misstated the renewal rents. HexFed sued in April 2021 for a declaration that it had renewed and for breach of the covenant of quiet enjoyment. CBS Holdings counterclaimed for breach of contract, ejectment and unjust enrichment and sought a landlord's lien.

Following a December 18, 2023 bench trial, the Madison Circuit Court ruled for HexFed on all claims and counterclaims. It found CBS Holdings had waived its 12-month argument by accepting rent without objection and by signing a 2020 lease amendment without changing the term, reformed the lease to correct the parties' mutual mistake on the maximum rent, declared that HexFed had properly renewed, and awarded HexFed costs and attorneys' fees in an amount to be set later. The Alabama Supreme Court affirmed on October 18, 2024 (No. SC-2024-0077), holding among other things that the miscalculated rent in the renewal notice did not void a renewal sent with the required 90 days' written notice. It overruled CBS Holdings' application for rehearing on December 20, 2024.

On April 16, 2024, after a hearing, the trial court awarded HexFed $174,987.45 in costs and attorneys' fees in a short order. CBS Holdings appealed, arguing that HexFed's invoices, with 449 of 458 charges fully redacted on privilege grounds, did not let the court judge whether the work was reasonable and necessary. On July 11, 2025 (No. SC-2024-0308), the Alabama Supreme Court agreed in an opinion by Justice Cook, holding that a fee application based on time spent must describe the billed work well enough for the court to calculate a fee, and that the order must show how the court calculated the award and considered the Peebles factors. It reversed and remanded with instructions. Justice Sellers, joined by Justices Wise and Bryan, concurred in the result.

The lease dispute itself was resolved in HexFed's favor, with the trial court declaring HexFed entitled to occupy the space through at least March 31, 2026. What remained on remand was the amount of costs and fees CBS Holdings must pay.

timeline.label: CBS Holdings buys the building and takes over the lease
HexFed sues CBS Holdings in Madison Circuit Court over the lease renewal
Trial court rules for HexFed on all claims and reforms the lease
Trial court awards HexFed $174,987.45 in costs and attorney fees
Alabama Supreme Court affirms the merits judgment for HexFed (SC-2024-0077); rehearing overruled December 20, 2024
Alabama Supreme Court reverses the fee award over inadequate billing support and remands (SC-2024-0308)
